content.user_title: Improve React Components With Proven Patterns
content.value_statement: React code often overuses Effects and spreads state logic across components. This skill gives practical patterns for hooks, refs, composition, and state ownership.
actual_capabilities: Guides when to use event handlers instead of Effects.
Explains derived state, useMemo, and key-based reset patterns.
Provides examples for Effect dependencies and cleanup.
Recommends safe ref usage and custom hook naming.
Covers composition, controlled components, and compound components.
limitations: Does not run, test, or lint React code automatically.
Focuses on component patterns, not backend or deployment design.
Does not replace official React documentation for API edge cases.
Type design guidance may require a separate TypeScript skill.

use_cases.title: Review Component Effects
use_cases.description: Identify Effects that should become render calculations, event handlers, or key-based resets.

use_cases.title: Design Reusable UI Components
use_cases.description: Choose controlled, uncontrolled, compound, or composed component patterns for reusable interfaces.

use_cases.title: Coach React Code Reviews
use_cases.description: Create clear review feedback about hook dependencies, refs, and component ownership.

prompt_templates.title: Check One Component
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a single file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this React component for common Effect, state, and ref issues. Explain each issue in simple terms.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Effects
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate cleanup of existing hook logic.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find Effects that can be replaced with render calculations, event handlers, or key resets. Suggest a safer structure.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Component Composition
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare controlled, uncontrolled, compound, and composed patterns for this component family. Recommend the most maintainable design.

prompt_templates.title: Audit React Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit these related React components for state ownership, provider boundaries, custom hooks, refs, and Effect dependencies.

output_examples.input: A component stores fullName in state and updates it from firstName and lastName with an Effect.
output_examples.output: The output explains that fullName is derived state. It recommends calculating it during render and removing the Effect.

output_examples.input: A chat component reconnects whenever messages changes because the Effect depends on the messages array.
output_examples.output: The output recommends an updater function for setMessages and narrows the Effect dependencies to connection inputs.

output_examples.input: A reusable panel accepts many boolean props to switch large UI sections.
output_examples.output: The output identifies a composition issue and suggests separate composed components or a compound component interface.

best_practices: Calculate derived values during render before adding state or Effects.
Use Effects only to synchronize with external systems and always handle cleanup.
Prefer composition and explicit ownership over large prop-driven component switches.
anti_patterns: Using Effects for user event logic that belongs in event handlers.
Suppressing hook dependency lint warnings instead of fixing stale closures.
Building config-array UI frameworks when direct JSX would be clearer.

faq.question: Does this skill modify my React files automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples that an AI coding assistant can apply when editing with your approval.

faq.question: Which React topics does it emphasize?
faq.answer: It emphasizes Effects, dependencies, refs, custom hooks, component composition, and state ownership.

faq.question: Is this useful for TypeScript React projects?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance works with TypeScript React, but detailed type modeling is outside this skill.

faq.question: Can it help reduce unnecessary Effects?
faq.answer: Yes. It gives alternatives such as render calculations, event handlers, key resets, and updater functions.

faq.question: Does it cover testing React components?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on component implementation patterns and does not provide testing framework guidance.

faq.question: Does it require external services?
faq.answer: No. The skill is documentation-only and does not require network calls, scripts, or external services.
